design_boundary: Exact pointed Hebrew source forms remain source evidence; the proposed Roman forms record ordinary contact-language pronunciation rather than silently respelling the sources.

The initial executable probe uses a reversible phonemic Hebrew-script profile. Exact Hebrew spelling remains source evidence and a source-facing alternative; choosing a later etymographic or morphographic running-text convention is still open.
For ordinary contact vocabulary, consonantal yod is y, shin is š, het is x, and qoph is k; source r, d, and g remain distinct.

Ordinary contact vocabulary does not preserve dagesh-forte gemination, does not pronounce nonphonemic word-edge aleph or final he, and does not insert a vowel merely because a written sheva is present.
The bounded current coda rule maps source-final v to w only in the reviewed forms aw, xalaw, and lew; it is not yet a productive rule for unreviewed vocabulary.
Source lexical stress must be stored separately when stress becomes a modeled field; this packet does not posit a global contact-language stress shift.

These ordinary lexical decisions do not automatically govern the separate Biblical narrative source profile. Wayyiqtol, weqatal, narrative waw, discourse sequencing, and their intended interaction with Algonquian obviation require their own source-grounded construction decisions.

A hybrid_input_candidate identifies an approved lexical input and design direction, not a licensed hybrid output. No possessive or stative morphology may be attached until the receiving paradigm is sourced and adopted.
